description: Citizenship in the Nation covers how the United States is governed — the Constitution, the three branches, founding documents and national issues — and connects them to your own life through speeches, landmarks and a letter to your representatives.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)
Citizenship in the Nation Digital Resource Guide (scouting.org)

requirements.title: The Constitution
requirements.summary: What the Constitution is and what it does.

requirements.title: The Preamble
requirements.summary: The six purposes stated in the Preamble and how they affect your family and community.

requirements.title: The three branches
requirements.summary: The functions of the three branches of government and how they balance each other.

children.title: What each branch does
children.summary: The function of each branch of the federal government.

children.title: Separation of powers
children.summary: Why powers are divided among the branches.

children.title: Checks and balances
children.summary: How each branch checks the others.

children.title: Getting involved
children.summary: How citizens can take part in each branch.

requirements.title: Founding documents
requirements.summary: Important national documents and ideals, such as the Declaration of Independence, the Bill of Rights and the national motto.

children.title: The Declaration of Independence
children.summary: The purpose and meaning of the Declaration of Independence.

children.title: The Bill of Rights
children.summary: The Bill of Rights and the Fourteenth Amendment.

requirements.title: Following national issues
requirements.summary: Following the news for several days, discussing national issues and how one affects you, your family and community.

requirements.title: A historic speech
requirements.summary: Studying an approved historic speech: its author, context, content and importance.

requirements.title: National landmarks
requirements.summary: Two of four options, such as visiting a historic landmark, touring a capitol or federal facility, or researching a national monument.

children.title: Historic site

children.title: Capitol building
children.summary: Touring your state or federal capitol.

requirements.title: Writing to Congress
requirements.summary: Identifying your members of Congress and writing to one about a national issue.
